summary: The recorded base reproduces the reported Draft 2020-12 rejection of required:null. The exact candidate removes that null sentinel through the real request normalization path, passes its regressions, and passes independent tool-index-17 and boundary cases without hiding other malformed non-null required values.

tests.what_was_measured: Prepared-base source import paths and exact failure: required:null remained and raised 'None is not of type array'.
Candidate normalization regression suite: 27 tests and 3 subtests passed.
An 18-tool request with required:null at index 17 was accepted; nested null was removed; valid arrays were preserved; malformed non-null required remained rejected; properties:null remained rejected.
Two trailing-whitespace findings, both in candidate-retained raw pytest output files rather than source or tests.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 was visible through rocminfo and Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, but the defect is CPU-side request schema validation and no inference or GPU numerical claim was needed.

remaining_counterexamples: A tool schema containing properties:null still fails Draft 2020-12 validation with None is not of type 'object'; this is a neighboring malformed-schema case, not the original required:null error.
remaining_limitations: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 weights and the complete original request body were unavailable, so no full-model, semantic, distributed, or original-deployment reproduction was performed.
No end-to-end HTTP server was started; the actual OpenAIServingChat._validate_request path was exercised directly.
No native rebuild was applicable because the candidate changes only Python source and Python tests.
The candidate contains trailing whitespace in two raw log artifacts reported by git diff --check.
